blocker: The register-contract violation is proven end to end, but the confidentiality claim that would give this defect security impact was tested and did not hold. The plausible reading of these sixteen arms is that they expose the AES initial key shares, which would be key recovery because src/aes/data/aes.rdl and src/aes/rtl/aes_core.sv:480 both state the initial key is share 0 XORed with share 1. It was measured directly, on the full aes block with the real aes_core attached and the key shares confirmed loaded, and it is false: the arms read the subreg_ext q port, which src/caliptra_prim/rtl/caliptra_prim_subreg_ext.sv:28 drives from wd, so the response is a combinational echo of the requester's own A-channel data. The stored shares reach only the qs port, which src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:298 leaves unconnected on these sixteen instances, so no arm in this multiplexer could return them. What remains proven is that sixteen addresses the audited tree declares sw = w return non-zero data instead of the constant zero the same file's addr_hit[0] arm uses, and that the data is the reader's own bus content. That is a violation of the declared software access policy and a register-model divergence, with no demonstrated loss of confidentiality, integrity or availability. The case is filed at that boundary rather than at the key-disclosure claim.
proof_method_executed: Thirty-two scripted structural gates over the submitted checkout, a directed VCS W-2024.09-SP1 simulation of one unmodified aes block elaborated through the project's own src/aes/config/aes.vf filelist and driven only over its TileLink register interface, and a negative control that rewrites the sixteen defective read arms to constant zero on a scratch copy of aes_reg_top.sv and re-runs the identical testbench.
result_summary: One whole aes block was driven over TileLink only, with offsets taken from the generated register package. AES_STATUS.IDLE was polled until set, reading 0x00000011 after two polls, which satisfies the RDL precondition that key registers can only be updated while the unit is idle. The sixteen KEY_SHARE0 and KEY_SHARE1 words were then written with per-word distinct patterns based on 0xA5A50000 and 0x5A5A0000, with no bus error. The IV address, declared sw = rw and read through iv_0_qs, returned 0x5A8E97D9, which differs from the 0xDEADBEEF filler held on the A channel and so establishes that a hardware-backed readback is observable in this same DUT. Reads of the first and last word of each share then returned 0xDEADBEEF on all four addresses, equal to the filler and not to any written pattern. A second read of the first share-0 address with 0x21524110 on a_data returned 0x21524110. The response therefore tracks the requester's own A-channel data and contains no key material. No bus error was raised anywhere in the run.
security_impact_assessment: A register-model and access-policy divergence with no demonstrated confidentiality, integrity or availability impact, which is why the CVSS base score is 0.0 rather than a rounded-up guess. Sixteen addresses that the audited tree's own register description declares write-only answer reads with non-zero data, where the same generated file uses constant zero for that case at addr_hit[0]. Software, a register model generated from the RDL, or any conformance test that asserts write-only-reads-zero will disagree with the hardware here. The reason the impact stops there is structural and worth stating precisely, because it is also what a reviewer will want to check: the defective arms read reg2hw.key_share*.q, and src/caliptra_prim/rtl/caliptra_prim_subreg_ext.sv is purely combinational with q = wd and qs = d, so q carries the bus write data and qs carries the hardware value. On these sixteen instances the qs port is left unconnected at src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:298 and no key_share*_qs signal exists in the file at all, so the loaded shares in key_init_q have no route into this multiplexer. The exposure is a combinational echo confined to the requesting transaction: a reader learns only what it placed on the bus itself, and cannot learn what another agent wrote earlier, because nothing stores wd between transactions. The residual concern is defence in depth. The write-only declaration exists so that the key registers have no read path at all, and this defect creates one; it returns the wrong source today, and any later change that connected qs, or any reuse of this arm pattern on a register whose q does reflect stored state, would convert it into a disclosure without touching the line that is wrong.

evidence.key_observation: On the unmodified tree, with status=0x00000011 after idle_polls=2 and write_err_seen=0: s0_0=0xdeadbeef, s0_7=0xdeadbeef, s1_0=0xdeadbeef, s1_7=0xdeadbeef against filler 0xdeadbeef and written patterns 0xa5a50001, 0xa5a50008, 0x5a5a0001, 0x5a5a0008. Re-reading the first address with a different filler gave s0_0_alt=0x21524110 for alt_filler=0x21524110. The IV control read iv0_readback=0x5a8e97d9, differing from the filler. Verdict line SUMMARY checks=10 fails=4 witness_hits=2 with core_idle=1, share0_exposed=1, share1_exposed=1, iv_hw_path=1, echo=1. Four write-only addresses return data instead of zero, and that data is the requester's own bus content rather than the stored shares.
evidence.negative_evidence: With the mitigation applied to a scratch copy, rewriting all sixteen arms to reg_rdata_next[31:0] = '0, the same testbench measured s0_0=s0_7=s1_0=s1_7=0x00000000 and s0_0_alt=0x00000000 while alt_filler was still 0x21524110, so the readback stopped tracking the request. The four invariant checks went from CHECK_FAIL to CHECK_PASS, witness_hits fell from 2 to 0, share0_exposed and share1_exposed fell to 0, and PROOF_RESULT went to FAIL. The idle precondition, the no-error containment and the IV control were byte-identical across both runs, at status=0x00000011, idle_polls=2 and iv0_readback=0x5a8e97d9, so the only variable that moved is the one named in the claim.

evidence_items: src/aes/data/aes.rdl:8 and src/aes/data/aes.rdl:27 declare every KEY_SHARE0 and KEY_SHARE1 field sw = w, and src/aes/data/aes.rdl:24 and :43 place the two arrays at 0x04 and 0x24. This is the audited tree's own statement of the access policy.
src/aes/data/aes.rdl:46 declares the adjacent IV fields sw = rw, which is what makes the write-only declaration on the key shares a deliberate distinction rather than a default.

src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:1735-1765 assigns reg_rdata_next[31:0] from reg2hw.key_share0[i].q and reg2hw.key_share1[i].q on all sixteen addresses; exactly sixteen such assignments exist in the file. src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:125 drives the bus read data straight from reg_rdata_next.

src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:1731-1733 shows the same case statement driving reg_rdata_next bits to constant '0 on addr_hit[0], and src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:1768 shows it reading iv_0_qs on the IV address. Eight arms in the file read a *_qs hardware value, so both correct shapes were available.

src/caliptra_prim/rtl/caliptra_prim_subreg_ext.sv:28 assigns q = wd and :27 assigns qs = d, and the module contains no always_ff, so q is a combinational function of the write data and holds no state between transactions.

src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:292 feeds u_key_share0_0.wd from key_share0_0_wd, src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:1569 assigns that signal from reg_wdata, and src/caliptra_tlul/rtl/caliptra_tlul_adapter_reg.sv:84 assigns wdata_o from tl_i.a_data. This is the full path from the requester's A channel to the read response.

src/aes/rtl/aes_core.sv:1028-1029 drives hw2reg.key_share0[i].d and hw2reg.key_share1[i].d from key_init_q, the registers holding the loaded shares, and src/aes/rtl/aes_core.sv:480 forms the cipher key as key_init_q[0] ^ key_init_q[1]. That is the value a disclosure would have to carry.

src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:298 leaves u_key_share0_0.qs unconnected and no key_share*_qs signal exists anywhere in the file, whereas src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:634 wires u_iv_0.qs out to iv_0_qs. The stored shares therefore have no wire into the read multiplexer, which bounds the defect structurally and not only by measurement.
All sixteen key-share instances are tied to .re (1'b0), so reading these addresses raises no register-side read effect and the observation is non-perturbing.

src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_pkg.sv:268 places AES_KEY_SHARE0_0_OFFSET at 4, matching the RDL, and the block exposes AES_KEY_SHARE1_0_OFFSET and AES_STATUS_OFFSET likewise, so every address the witness uses is a software-visible offset from the generated package rather than an assumed one.
No privilege, lifecycle or debug qualifier appears anywhere in src/aes/rtl/aes_reg_top.sv:1735-1765, so the read is available at the lowest privilege level that can reach the block.
non_findings: This is not a key disclosure. The claim was tested on the full aes block with the shares confirmed loaded and the core idle, and the readback carried the requester's own A-channel data on every one of the four sampled addresses, changing when the A-channel value changed. The written patterns never appeared. Reporting this case as exposing the AES initial key would misstate what the hardware does.
This is not a claim about the write path. onwrite = woclr and the sixteen write enables are unaffected; only the read response is defective.

This is not a finding about the IV registers. They are declared sw = rw and their arms read a hardware value, so they serve here as the control proving a hardware-backed readback is observable in the same DUT.
This is not a claim that the read perturbs AES state, since all sixteen instances tie re to 1'b0.

This is not a claim about aes_reg_top in isolation. A standalone build of that module cannot answer the disclosure question at all, because hw2reg would be a testbench input; the whole-block build is what makes the boundary measurable.

reproduction.tools: VCS W-2024.09-SP1 at /data0/tools/Synopsys/vcs/vcs/W-2024.09-SP1/bin, bash, python3. CALIPTRA_ROOT points at the submitted checkout, CALIPTRA_PRIM_ROOT at src/caliptra_prim_generic, CALIPTRA_PRIM_MODULE_PREFIX is caliptra_prim_generic. The design is compiled with +define+CALIPTRA_MODE_SUBSYSTEM.
reproduction.success_marker: PROOF_RESULT: PASS from the simulation script, result=PASS with structural_gates_passed=32/32 from the structural audit, NEGATIVE_CONTROL: PASS from the negative control.
reproduction.determinism: Fully deterministic. The stimulus is a fixed directed TileLink sequence with no randomization and no seed dependence. Bus transactions are driven from tasks that wait for the a_ready and d_valid handshakes rather than counting cycles, and the idle precondition is polled rather than assumed, so no measurement depends on event ordering within a time slot. The EDN responder returns a fixed pattern and no observation depends on entropy values.
reproduction.note_on_verdict_markers: The testbench prints result=PASS only on success. Its failure branch prints PROOF_RESULT: FAIL with no result= line, because the negative control run is supposed to reach that branch and a bare result=FAIL would be read as a real failure by the log scanners.
reproduction.note_on_filelist: The simulation script expands src/aes/config/aes.vf with two adjustments that change neither the set of files compiled nor their contents: it appends an include path for the generated register headers, which src/aes/rtl/aes_clp_wrapper.sv requires but which the list does not carry, and it emits packages ahead of modules because the list places some modules before the packages they import.
reproduction.note_on_log_order: The negative control invokes the simulation script with a DUT override, so it overwrites run.log and witness.log. The unmodified-tree simulation is re-run last so the submitted logs describe the audited RTL, with the negative control's own output preserved in negative_control.log.

conclusion: The defect is confirmed and reproducible. The read-response multiplexer in aes_reg_top returns register-path content on all sixteen KEY_SHARE0 and KEY_SHARE1 addresses, which the audited tree's own register description declares write-only and which the same generated case statement handles with constant zero elsewhere. Rewriting the sixteen arms to constant zero flips the measurement while leaving every control byte-identical, which establishes non-vacuity. It is filed as partial_proof because the impact is narrower than the defect first appears: the arms read the subreg_ext q port, which is the bus write data rather than the hardware value, and the qs port carrying the loaded shares is left unconnected on these instances, so the response is a combinational echo of the requester's own transaction and no key material leaves the block. The correct claim is a violation of the declared write-only access policy plus a register-model divergence and a read path that should not exist, scored at a 0.0 CVSS base because no confidentiality, integrity or availability loss was demonstrated. The key-recovery reading was explicitly tested and is recorded as an excluded non-finding with the RTL lines that bound it.
